html:
The Jabirr Jabirr are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Dampier Peninsula in the Kimberley of Western Australia, on the coast north of Broome. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

They are saltwater people, living by fishing, shellfish and hunting along the coast. Their neighbours were the Nyulnyul to the north, the Ngumbarl and Djugun to the south and the Nimanburu to the east. The English buccaneer William Dampier beached his ship on this peninsula in 1688. From the 1860s pearling boats worked these waters and often forced Aboriginal men and women to dive for shell. Their language, Jabirr Jabirr, belongs to the Nyulnyulan family.
